# Body Scope

## How To Build

A BodyScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A BodyScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

The main window's body: the area to the right of the project sidebar, where the tasks sent to the harness, and the files opened in tabs beside them, are shown, and the chat input they are sent from.

### Shape

#### Description

Beneath the [RibbonScope](../../ui/components/ribbon/index.md#ribbon-scope), to the right of the [ProjectSidebarScope](../../ui/components/project-sidebar/index.md#project-sidebar-scope), which runs the full height beside it, and reaching the window's right edge. It is part of the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor).
The [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) lives within the body, along its bottom: its left edge against the project sidebar, and above it, beneath the body's tab bar, the selected tab's contents: the message list, or an open file. While a task runs, the [RightSidebarScope](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar-scope) runs the body's full height at its right, beside the tab bar, the selected tab's contents, and the chat input, and the chat input's right edge is against it: the chat input never runs beneath the right sidebar. While that sidebar isn't there, the chat input reaches the window's right edge.

#### Contents

Everything that can be in the body:

- a tab bar along its top, holding a Chat tab and a tab for each file open
- the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list), the chat history, shown beneath the tab bar while the Chat tab is selected
- the hint shown in the message list's place before any task has been sent, or while no project is open, as the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor) and the [NoProjectStateScope](../no-project/index.md#no-project-state-scope) say
- an [EditorScope](../editor/index.md#editor-scope) for each open file, shown beneath the tab bar while its tab is selected
- the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), along the bottom beneath whichever tab is selected
- the [RightSidebarScope](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar-scope), at the right of all of these, the tab bar and the chat input included, while a task runs

An [InsetPanelScope](../../ui/components/inset-panel/index.md#inset-panel-scope) floats over the whole window, the body included, but is never part of it.

#### Tabs

Along the top of the body runs a tab bar, in gpui-kit's default tab styling, across the width the message list takes: from the project sidebar to the right sidebar while a task runs, and to the window's right edge otherwise. Its first tab, Chat, shows the message list, and is always there: it can't be closed or moved. After it comes a tab for each open file, in the order they were opened, scrolling sideways once there are more than fit.
Just one tab's contents show at a time, filling the space between the tab bar and the chat input. The chat input stays along the bottom whichever tab is selected, so a prompt can be written while a file shows. The body starts with Chat selected, and clicking a tab selects it.
A file's tab shows the file's name, then, while it has unsaved changes, a dot, and at its right a small close button. Hovering it shows the file's path in the project as its tooltip.

#### Open File

A file opened, from the [FileTreeScope](../../ui/components/file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope) or anywhere else the [OpenFileScope](../open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) says, shows in an [EditorScope](../editor/index.md#editor-scope) in a tab of its own, as many files open at once as are opened. A file not open yet gets a new tab, just after the one selected, and is selected. Opening a file that already has a tab selects that tab instead, leaving its editor as it was, unsaved changes and all.
Nothing slides: a file's tab is selected, and its editor shows, at once, and closing it takes it away at once too. There is no split, and no edge to drag; the file takes the tab bar's full width above the chat input.
Closing a file's tab, with its close button or the editor's, closes the file, the editor first asking to discard any unsaved changes. Closing the selected tab selects the tab to its right, or, with none to its right, the one to its left, which is Chat once no file is left. Closing a tab that isn't selected leaves the selection as it is.

content.text:
The body's Chat tab now shows a small spinner at its right while a run is under way, and it goes away once nothing is running. The build succeeds and the 22 tab-related tests pass. I didn't launch the app to look at it, and no test checks the spinner itself.

- **When it shows:** while a Code, Chain or Spec task runs, or while an Ask question runs. You said "task", but I counted Ask questions too because they also run under the Chat tab. If you want tasks only, it's a one-line change to `chat_running()`.
- **How it's drawn:** it's gpui-kit's own `Spinner` in the same corner of the tab where file tabs have their close button, so it follows the default tab styling and the theme colours.

The change is in `src/prompt_mode.rs`: a new `chat_running()` helper and the Chat tab in `render_tabs()`.

The spec doesn't mention this spinner. I left `./spec` alone as instructed, so you may want to add a line to the Tabs section of `spec/scope/application/Body.pi`.
